| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ὀψὲ δὲ δὴ μετέειπε γέρων ἱππηλάτα Φοῖνιξ (9.432, whole-line speech introduction) | "But late indeed spoke among them the old man, horse-driver Phoenix," | "At last Phoenix, the old horse-driver, spoke among them," | "answered" (nothing is answered), "addressed" (reserved for προσέφη); follows ὀψὲ δὲ δὴ μετέειπε βοὴν ἀγαθὸς Διομήδης (7.399) and γέρων ἱππηλάτα (7.125) |
| δάκρυ’ ἀναπρήσας (9.433; ἀναπρήθω rare, root not certain) | "tears bursting forth" | "bursting into tears" (+ note: traditional sense, root uncertain) | "shedding tears" (loses the verb’s force), "blowing out tears", "kindling tears" (each picks one guess) |
| νήπιον (of the boy Achilles, 9.440) | "a child" | "a mere child" | "foolish" (the table’s νήπιος, which would call the boy a fool; the departure is that here the word means only "too young", and the note says that elsewhere it is "foolish"), "childish", "an infant" |
| ὁμοίϊος πόλεμος (9.440, ὁμοιΐου πολέμοιο) | "war common to all" | "the war that is common to all" | the Odyssey’s "even-handed war" (18.264); departure to follow the Iliad’s own rows νεῖκος ὁμοίϊον "a quarrel common to all" (4.444) and γῆρας ὁμοίϊον (4.315), since the same adjective is one word in this poem |
| ἀγορέων (9.441) | "assemblies" | "assemblies" | "councils", "debates"; ἀγορή "assembly" (1.490) |
| ῥητήρ · πρηκτήρ (9.443) | "a speaker" · "a doer" | "a speaker of words" · "a doer of deeds" | "orator" (a performance word), "master of speech"; "man of action", "achiever" |
| γῆρας ἀποξύσας … ἡβώοντα (9.446) | "having scraped off old age … in youthful prime" | "to scrape off my old age and make me young and in youthful prime" | "peeling off", "shedding", "flourishing youth"; ἀποξύω "scrape off", ἡβάω "be in youthful prime" (7.133) |
| παλλακίς (9.449, 9.452) | "a concubine" | "a concubine" | "mistress", "slave-girl"; καλλικόμοιο "fair-haired" as the Odyssey’s Ἑλένης καλλικόμοιο (15.58) |
| στυγερὰς Ἐρινῦς (9.454) | "hateful Erinyes" | "the hateful Erinyes" | "the Furies" (the Latin name), "dread" (reserved for δεινός); follows the Odyssey’s μητρὸς Ἐρινύες "a mother’s Erinyes" (11.280) |
| Ζεύς τε καταχθόνιος (9.457) | "Zeus beneath the earth" | "Zeus of the underworld" (+ note: Zeus as ruler of the dead) | "Hades" (the Greek withholds the name), "Zeus of the nether world", "infernal Zeus" |
| ἐπαινὴ Περσεφόνεια (9.457, 9.569) | "grim Persephone" | "grim Persephone" | the Odyssey table’s ἐπαινή "grim" (10.491), unchanged |
| ἔται καὶ ἀνεψιοί (9.464) | "kinsmen and cousins" | "kinsmen and cousins" | "clansmen", "relatives", "brothers" |
| θαλέθοντες ἀλοιφῇ (of pigs, 9.467) | "abundant with fat" | "abounding in fat" | "blooming", "thriving", "luscious"; θαλέθω is from the root of θαλερός "abundant" (8.476) |
| εὑόμενοι τανύοντο διὰ φλογὸς Ἡφαίστοιο (9.468) | "being singed, were stretched out through the flame of Hephaestus" | "were stretched out to be singed through the flame of Hephaestus" | "roasted" (εὕω is "singe"), "spitted"; Ἡφαίστοιο "flame of Hephaestus" as at 2.426 |
| κέραμος (9.469, ἐκ κεράμων) | "jars" | "jars" | "pots", "urns"; as in the table (5.387) |
| ἴαυον (9.470; ἰαύω) | "slept" | "slept" | "lay down", "kept their beds" |
| εὐερκής (αὐλῆς εὐερκέος, 9.472) | "well-fenced" | "well-fenced" | the Odyssey table’s εὐερκὴς αὐλή "well-fenced courtyard" (22.449), unchanged |
| προδόμῳ (9.473) | "fore-house" | "vestibule" | the Odyssey table’s πρόδομος (14.5), unchanged |
| θύρας πυκινῶς ἀραρυίας (9.475) | "the doors closely fitted" | "the closely fitted doors" | "tight-shut", "well-joined" (the adverb is "closely") |
| δμῳάς τε γυναῖκας (9.477) | "the maidservants, women" | "the maids" | "slave-women", "serving-women"; δμῳαί "maidservants" / "maids" (6.69) |
| μητέρα μήλων (9.479) | "mother of flocks" | "mother of flocks" | "nurse of flocks", "land of sheep"; μῆλα "flocks" as in ἴφια μῆλα |
| ἐσχατιή (9.484) | "the edge" | "the edge" | "the border", "the far end"; follows the Odyssey’s ἐπ’ ἐσχατιῇ "at the edge" (9.182) |
| θεοῖς ἐπιείκελ’ Ἀχιλλεῦ (9.485, 9.494, vocative) | "resembling the gods" | "like the gods" | "godlike" (reserved for ἀντίθεος), "equal to the gods"; follows the Odyssey table’s ἐπιείκελος ἀθανάτοισιν (4.394) |
| ὄψου … ἄσαιμι (9.489) | "should fill you with food" | "fed you full" | "relish", "meat", "dainties"; ὄψον is the dish eaten with bread, and the note says so |
| ἐν νηπιέῃ ἀλεγεινῇ (9.491) | "in your grievous infancy" | "in your grievous infancy" | "troublesome", "painful"; ἀλεγεινός "grievous" |
| θυμὸν μέγαν (9.496) | "great spirit" | "great spirit" | "great heart" (θυμός is "heart" elsewhere, and the departure is made because ἦτορ "heart" follows in the next unit, as the Odyssey table does at 8.204), "proud heart", "mighty heart" |
| στρεπτοὶ δέ τε καὶ θεοὶ αὐτοί (9.497) | "turnable are even the gods themselves" | "even the gods themselves can be turned" | "pliant", "moved by prayer", "changeable"; στρεπτός is "turnable" from τρέπω |
| ἀρετὴ τιμή τε βίη τε (9.498) | "excellence and honour and might" | "excellence, honour and might" | "virtue", "prowess", "strength" (reserved for κράτος); ἀρετή "excellence", βίη "might" |
| παρατρωπῶσι (9.500) | "turn aside" | "are turned aside" | "persuade", "move", "win over" |
| λιταί (9.502, personified) | "Prayers" | "Prayers" | "Entreaties", "Supplications", "Litai" (a transliteration); the note says λιτή is "prayer, entreaty" |
| χωλαί τε ῥυσαί τε παραβλῶπές τ’ ὀφθαλμώ (9.503) | "lame and wrinkled and asquint in the two eyes" | "lame and wrinkled and squinting with both eyes" | "limping", "crooked", "squint-eyed"; ὀφθαλμώ is a dual accusative and the note says so |
| ἄτη (personified, 9.505–512) | "Bewilderment" | "Bewilderment" | "Ruin", "Folly", "Delusion", "Blind Folly"; follows the Iliad’s ἄτη "bewilderment" (1.412, 9.115) and the Odyssey table’s ἀάω · ἄτη |
| ἀρτίπος (9.505) | "sound of foot" | "sound of foot" | "swift-footed", "sure-footed", "fleet" (reserved for ποδώκης); ἄρτιος "sound" + πούς |
| ἀναίνομαι (9.510, 9.585) | "reject" | "reject" | "refuse" (kept for ἀποείπῃ / ἀπεῖπον, 1.515), "deny", "scorn" |
| τῷ ἄτην ἅμ’ ἕπεσθαι (9.512) | "that Bewilderment go along with him" | "that Bewilderment go along with that man" | "attend him", "dog his steps" |
| ἐπιζάφελος χόλος (9.525) | "violent anger" | "furious anger" | "excessive", "overpowering"; follows the Odyssey’s ἐπιζαφελῶς "furiously" (6.330), and χόλος stays "anger" |
| δωρητοί τε πέλοντο παράρρητοί τ’ ἐπέεσσι (9.526) | "were to be won by gifts and to be talked round with words" | "could be won by gifts and talked round with words" | "bribed", "open to bribery", "placated"; the verbal adjectives δωρητός and παράρρητος |
| μενεχάρμης (Αἰτωλοὶ μενεχάρμαι, 9.529) | "steadfast in the fray" | "steadfast in the fray" | "staunch in battle", "stout in fight", "battle-eager" (reserved for μεμαώς); μένω "stand fast" + χάρμη "fight" |
| ἐνάριζον (9.530) | "slew" | "killing" | "stripped", "despoiled" (the verb strictly strips a slain man, and the note says so) |
| Ἄρηϊ (διαπραθέειν μεμαῶτες Ἄρηϊ, 9.532) | "in war" | "in war" | "with Ares", "to the god of war" (the name stands for war, and the note says so) |
| θαλύσια (9.534) | "first-fruits" | "first-fruits" | "harvest-offerings", "thank-offerings", "garlands"; the note says they are offerings of the first produce |
| γουνῷ ἀλωῆς (9.534; sense of γουνός not certain) | "on the rich ground of the orchard" | "on the rich ground of his orchard" (+ note: sense of γουνός uncertain) | "on the hill of", "on the slope of", "on the threshing-floor of"; ἀλωή "orchard" as shipped at Odyssey 6.293 |
| δαίνυνθ’ ἑκατόμβας (9.535) | "feasted on hecatombs" | "feasted on his hecatombs" | "dined on", "were honoured with"; ἑκατόμβη "hecatomb" (4.102) |
| ἀάσατο δὲ μέγα θυμῷ (9.537) | "was greatly bewildered in his heart" | "was greatly bewildered in his heart" | "blinded", "was deluded"; follows ἀασάμην "I was bewildered" (9.116) and the Odyssey table’s ἀάω "bewilder" |
| δῖον γένος (9.538, accusative of the object of anger) | "the heavenly race" | "the heavenly race" (+ note: the neuter ending is why it is not an epithet of the goddess) | "the divine offspring" (as an epithet of Artemis), "her heavenly kin" |
| χλούνην σῦν (9.539; χλούνης, meaning not known) | "a lone … boar" | "a lone … boar" (+ note: meaning of χλούνης not known, "solitary" the ancient guess) | "savage" (σῦν ἄγριον is "wild boar"), "rampaging", "castrated" |
| ἔθων (9.540; probably ἔθω "be accustomed") | "haunting" | "haunting" (+ note: traditional sense, not certain) | "ravaging", "frequenting", "roaming" |
| προθέλυμνα (9.541) | "torn up from the base" | "torn up from the base" | "uprooted entire", "root and all", "branch and root"; θέλυμνα are the roots or base of a tree |
| ἄνθεσι μήλων (9.542) | "the blossoms of the apples" | "the blossoms of their apples" | "of the flocks" (μῆλα, which this genitive plural is not), "apple-blossom" |
| θηρήτορας ἄνδρας (9.544) | "hunter men" | "hunters" | "huntsmen", "men skilled in the chase" |
| πυρῆς ἐπέβησ’ ἀλεγεινῆς (9.546) | "set upon the grievous pyre" | "put on the grievous pyre" | "sent to the sad pyre", "made mount the painful pyre"; ἀλεγεινός "grievous" (10.78) |
| ἀϋτὴν … κέλαδον (9.547) | "din and battle-cry" | "a great din and battle-cry" | "shouting", "clamour"; ἀϋτή "battle-cry" (4.328) |
| δέρμα λαχνῆεν (9.548) | "hairy hide" | "hairy hide" | "shaggy hide" (reserved for λάσιος), "bristling"; λαχνήεις "hairy" (2.743) |
| ἄρηι φίλος (9.550) | "dear to Ares" | "dear to Ares" | "beloved of war", "war-loving"; follows ἀρηΐφιλος "dear to Ares" (2.778) |
| ὄφρα … τόφρα (9.550–551) | "so long as … for that time" | "as long as … (it went badly for)" | "meanwhile", "then" (the Odyssey table’s τόφρα row, 8.438 and 8.453), "so long" |
| πύκα περ φρονεόντων (9.554) | "though they think shrewdly" | "who are shrewd of thought" | "though they are wise" (reserved for πεπνυμένος), "though they have sense" |
| μνηστῇ ἀλόχῳ (9.556) | "wedded wife" | "wedded wife" | "betrothed", "bride"; follows the table’s μνηστῇς ἀλόχοισι "wedded wives" (6.246) |
| κάρτιστος ἐπιχθονίων … ἀνδρῶν (9.558) | "strongest of men upon the earth" | "the strongest of the men then living on earth" | "mightiest" (reserved for ἴφθιμος), "best"; κάρτιστος "strongest" (1.266), ἐπιχθόνιοι ἄνθρωποι "men upon the earth" (Odyssey 8.479) |
| νύμφη (of a girl, 9.560) | "bride" | "bride" | "nymph", "maiden" (reserved for κούρη); the note says νύμφη is a young woman here |
| ἐπώνυμον (9.562) | "as a by-name" | "as a surname" | "in honour of", "for her name"; ἐπώνυμος "named after" |
| πολυπενθής (ἀλκυόνος πολυπενθέος, 9.563) | "much-grieving" | "much-grieving" | "much-sorrowing", "full of woe"; πένθος "grief" |
| χόλον θυμαλγέα πέσσων (9.565) | "brooding heart-paining anger" | "brooding his heart-paining anger" | "digesting", "nursing", "heart-grieving"; πέσσω "cook, digest" is "brood over" here |
| ἐξ ἀρέων μητρός (9.566) | "by the curses of his mother" | "by his mother’s curses" | "prayers" (for ἀρά the note gives both), "vows" |
| γαῖαν πολυφόρβην (9.568) | "the much-nourishing earth" | "the much-nourishing earth" | "all-feeding", "bountiful", "grain-giving" (reserved for ζείδωρος); πολύς + φορβή "food" |
| πρόχνυ καθεζομένη (9.570) | "kneeling forward" | "kneeling forward" | "sitting forward", "bent low" |
| δεύοντο δὲ δάκρυσι κόλποι (9.570) | "with tears her lap was wet" | "her lap was wet with tears" | "her bosom", "her robe"; κόλπος "lap" |
| ἠεροφοῖτις Ἐρινύς (9.571) | "the mist-walking Erinys" | "the Erinys who walks in the mist" | "that walks in darkness", "air-roaming", "who wanders in gloom"; ἠέρι "mist" as in ἐρεβεννὴ ἀήρ "murky mist" (5.864) |
| ἀμείλιχον ἦτορ (9.572) | "an ungentle heart" | "an unrelenting heart" | "implacable", "pitiless" (reserved for νηλεής); follows the table’s ἀμείλιχος "ungentle" / "unrelenting" (9.158) |
| ὅμαδος καὶ δοῦπος (9.573) | "the din and thud" | "the uproar and the thud" | "the clamour and the crash", "the roar"; ὅμαδος "din", δοῦπος "thud" |
| θεῶν ἱερῆας ἀρίστους (9.575) | "the best priests of the gods" | "the best priests of the gods" | "chief priests", "noblest"; ἱερεύς "priest" (1.23) |
| τέμενος περικαλλές … πεντηκοντόγυον (9.578–579) | "a very fair precinct … of fifty gyes" | "a very fair estate of fifty acres" (+ note: γύης a land measure of unknown size) | "fifty-acre" as certain, "of fifty ploughlands"; τέμενος "precinct" in `l` and "estate" in `i` (6.194), περικαλλής "very fair" |
| οἰνοπέδοιο · ψιλὴν ἄροσιν (9.579–580) | "vine-land" · "bare ploughland" | "vineyard land" · "bare ploughland" | "wine-ground", "naked", "open"; ψιλός "bare" |
| ὑψηρεφέος θαλάμοιο (9.582) | "the high-roofed chamber" | "the high-roofed chamber" | "lofty-roofed", "vaulted"; follows the Odyssey’s ὑψερεφές "high-roofed" (4.15) |
| κολλητὰς σανίδας (9.583) | "close-joined doors" | "close-joined doors" | "glued boards", "well-fitted planks"; σανίς "board" |
| κεδνότατοι καὶ φίλτατοι (9.586) | "most trusty and dearest" | "the most trusty and the dearest" | "most faithful", "most loyal"; follows the Odyssey’s κεδνός "trusty" (10.8) |
| θάλαμος πύκ’ ἐβάλλετο (9.588) | "the chamber was thickly struck" | "his chamber was being thickly pelted" | "was battered", "was shaken"; πύκα "thickly" |
| ἐΰζωνος παράκοιτις (9.590) | "well-girdled consort" | "well-girdled wife" | "fair-girdled" (reserved for καλλίζωνος), "fair-belted"; follows the table’s ἐϋζώνοιο γυναικός (1.429) and παράκοιτις "consort" / "wife" (4.60) |
| κήδεα (9.592) | "sorrows" | "sorrows" | "troubles", "woes"; follows the table’s κήδεα "sorrows" (1.445) |
| πόλιν δέ τε πῦρ ἀμαθύνει (9.593) | "the city fire levels to dust" | "fire reduces the city to dust" | "burns down", "destroys"; ἀμαθύνω from ἄμαθος "sand, dust" |
| βαθυζώνους γυναῖκας (9.594) | "deep-girdled women" | "deep-girdled women" | "deep-bosomed" (reserved for βαθύκολπος), "fair-girdled", "low-belted"; βαθύς "deep" + ζώνη "girdle", the picture uncertain |
| χροῒ δ’ ἔντε’ ἐδύσετο παμφανόωντα (9.596) | "on his skin the gear he put, all-shining" | "put the all-shining gear on his body" | "armour" (reserved for τεύχεα), "dazzling"; ἔντεα "gear" (3.339), παμφανόων "all-shining" (5.295) |
| κακὸν ἦμαρ ἀπαμύνω (9.597) | "warded off the evil day" | "warded off the evil day from" | "averted", "kept off"; ἀμύνω "ward off" |
| δῶρα τέλεσσαν (9.598) | "paid the gifts" | "gave him the gifts" | "fulfilled", "delivered"; τελέω "pay, fulfil" |
| κακὸν ἤμυνε καὶ αὔτως (9.599) | "he warded off the evil even so" | "he warded off the evil even so, without them" | "for nothing" (the table’s αὔτως "just so" in `l`, 2.342, with `i` taking the sense the clause needs), "in vain" |
| μή … δαίμων ἐνταῦθα τρέψειε φίλος (9.600–601) | "nor let a divinity turn you that way, dear friend" | "let no divinity turn you that way, my friend" | "god", "spirit", "demon"; δαίμων "divinity" (3.420), and the note says φίλος is taken as the vocative |
| κάκιον … νηυσὶν καιομένῃσιν ἀμυνέμεν (9.601–602) | "worse … to defend ships when they are burning" | "worse to defend the ships once they are burning" | "to save", "to rescue" |
| ἐπὶ δώρων ἔρχεο (9.602–603) | "for the gifts go" | "go for the gifts" | "go to the gifts", "go on account of the gifts" (the note says the force of ἐπί is hard to pin down) |
| ἶσον … θεῷ τίσουσιν Ἀχαιοί (9.603) | "equally to a god will they honour you, the Achaeans" | "the Achaeans will honour you as they would a god" | "pay", "reward", "esteem"; τίω "honour" (1.508) |
| πόλεμον φθισήνορα (9.604) | "man-wasting war" | "the war that wastes men" | the table’s φθισήνωρ "man-wasting" / "that wastes men" (2.833), unchanged |
| οὐκέθ’ ὁμῶς τιμῆς ἔσεαι (9.605) | "no longer equally in honour will you be" | "you will no longer be held in the same honour" | "of equal honour", "honoured less"; τιμή "honour" |
